correctness.rationale: The count decomposes by least-significant block position into functions \(F_q(N)=q\lfloor N/(2^rq)\rfloor+\max\{0,(N\bmod 2^rq)-(2^rq-q)\}\). The residue interval is the terminal interval of each period, and the three possible locations of the two residuals give superadditivity of every \(F_q\); summing the finitely many active positions proves the theorem. The equality strip follows because prepending the top binary one creates a crossing \(1^r\) block only after the stated threshold. A fresh independent brute-force replay for \(2\le r\le5\), all addends through 100, and dyadic equality strips through exponent eight found no violations.
risks: The one-position argument uses the terminal residue interval special to all-one blocks and does not extend automatically to arbitrary words.
